groups.title: App Router Fundamentals
groups.question: You are structuring a Next.js app with a marketing site, a dashboard with a persistent sidebar and product pages by id. Explain how the App Router maps this.

followUps.File-system routing and the app director: How does the app directory turn folders into URLs?
followUps.Nested layouts and shared UI segments: Why does a layout keep its state when you navigate between child pages?

evidence.text: Each folder is a URL segment.
A folder becomes a reachable route when it has a page file.
The URL structure can be read directly from the folder tree.
A layout wraps all pages in its segment.
It stays mounted when navigating between those pages, so its state is kept.
This is how persistent sidebars and headers are built.
[id] matches one segment and passes it as a parameter.
[...slug] matches any number of segments.
They power pages like products, blog posts and docs.

groups.title: Navigation and Route Organization
groups.question: Your marketing pages and dashboard need different layouts without changing URLs, and slow pages should show a loading state. Explain how you would organise this.

followUps.Route groups for layout organisation: What does wrapping a folder name in parentheses do?
followUps.loading.tsx and error.tsx boundary files: What do loading.tsx and error.tsx add to a route?

evidence.text: A route group organises folders without adding to the URL.
Each group can have its own layout.
Marketing pages and the dashboard can use different layouts at the same URL level.
loading.tsx wraps the segment in Suspense and shows a fallback instantly.
error.tsx catches errors in the segment and shows a fallback with a retry.
Each only affects its own segment, so the rest of the page keeps working.

groups.title: Navigation in Practice
groups.question: You are building the dashboard's sidebar navigation, redirecting after a form submit and showing a photo in a modal that also has its own URL. Explain the navigation tools you would use.

followUps.Link component and programmatic navigati: What does Link do that a plain anchor does not, and how do you navigate from code?
followUps.usePathname and active link highlighting: How would you highlight the active link in the sidebar?
followUps.Parallel routes and intercepting routes: How do parallel and intercepting routes let a modal have its own URL?

evidence.text: Link prefetches routes in the background.
It navigates without a full reload.
useRouter from next/navigation navigates from code, such as after a form submit.

notEnough: Only saying Link is for navigation.

evidence.text: usePathname returns the current path.
Each link compares its href with the path.
Matching links get an active style.

notEnough: Only saying you add an active class.

evidence.text: Parallel routes render several pages in one layout at the same time.
Intercepting routes show a different UI, like a modal, when navigating within the app.
Opening the URL directly still shows the full page.

groups.title: Route Metadata and SEO
groups.question: Your product pages need good search results and link previews, and you want them built ahead of time. Explain how you would set metadata and pre-render the pages.

followUps.Metadata API for SEO and Open Graph: How would you set a unique title and preview for each product?

evidence.text: Pages export metadata or a generateMetadata function.
generateMetadata can fetch the product to build its title and description.
Open Graph tags control link previews on social sites.

notEnough: Only saying you set the title.

evidence.text: It returns the list of parameter values to build.
Those pages are rendered to static HTML at build time.
It suits known pages like blog posts, products and docs.

notEnough: Only saying it makes pages static.
